## Summary

Fixes #2301. The analysis covers all three production runs: [links-notation#315](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/319) (Claude Code 2.1.282), [browser-commander#106](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/konard/public-logs/main/tmp-hive-mind-log-upload-2nNBS9/08e10c4fbb284728/sanitized.log.txt) (2.1.284, 2.5 h, 15 subagents) and its [re-run](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/konard/97c3a1eb9c57b52512e3a999724cccf8/raw/6e1935a7b02d6a0efc1c6250b4985954debbc32f/tmp-hive-mind-log-upload-zYtTNW-sanitized.log.txt) (2.1.284, 44 min, 4 subagents). It also used the installed Claude binary and live reproductions.

### Exact root cause

Claude Code print mode waits for background tasks only up to `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (default 600000). The ceiling counts from the main thread's last message, not from the tasks' progress. In all three incidents, exactly 600 s after that message, it:

1. printed `Background tasks still running after 600s; terminating.` to stderr;
2. stopped every task, even subagents that were still working (in the re-run one had started `pytest` 2 s earlier, log line 155713);
3. gave the killed subagents synthetic `[Request interrupted by user]` and `The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use` results;
4. still emitted `result: success` (in the re-run, all three held-back results at once) and exited 0.

No user, permission prompt or tool classifier was involved. Hive Mind then let those **subagent-scoped** events (`parent_tool_use_id`) become the main session's final tool result. It reported `Final tool result failed … / Claude command failed with exit code 0` and never continued the work.

### Fixes

- **Background work stays enabled, with 4x the wait.** `solve` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=2400000` (40 min, 4x Claude Code's default; `HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` overrides it). It is deliberately not `0`, which would let one stuck task hang `solve` forever. The earlier `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_*` approach is removed.
- **Silent auto-resume when the ceiling is still hit.** The sweep is detected exactly (`src/claude.print-turn.lib.mjs`). This removes three false negatives:
  - stops that arrive before the `result`;
  - the stderr ceiling line was not recognised;
  - a background Bash is killed about 4 s after `result` with `killed.system=0`.

  `solve` then resumes the same session up to 5 times in a row (`HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_INCOMPLETE_TURN_MAX_RESUMES`). Each resume is only logged, with no PR comment or notice. The prompt tells the model that the ceiling (not a user) cancelled the work, lists the cancelled tasks with their partial output files, and asks it to redo only what is missing and to run long work in the foreground. The stale kill that Claude Code replays at the start of a `--resume` does not trigger another resume. A model's own `TaskStop` and later main-thread turns are handled correctly.
- **No false positives from subagents** (`src/claude.stream-events.lib.mjs`). Subagent tool errors, cancellations, last messages and compaction summaries no longer become the main session's verdict or summary; they are logged as diagnostics. The failure wording is now `Claude session failed (the CLI itself exited with code 0): …`.
- **OOM follow-ups (incident 1).** A failed session affected by a child OOM (`OOMKilled` + exit 1) is resumed through `--on-session-kill=resume`. The notice reports a new session only after it actually starts, and includes its ID. Telegram Docker tasks default to a 25% host-memory limit.
- The Claude prompt says that background work is allowed but only waited for within the ceiling after the turn ends, so long work belongs in the foreground.

The [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2301-1462dcec50ad/docs/case-studies/issue-2301/README.md) has:

- all three timelines with log line numbers;
- the binary evidence;
- an audit of every error and warning in the logs.

Most entries are expected or recoverable, such as the 46 worktree-guard refusals, the model's own command errors, and the `--attach-logs` security notice. It also has the compressed logs and upstream references.

**Upstream:** [anthropics/claude-code#98170](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/98170) is a focused report. It covers the idle-based ceiling killing working subagents, `success`/exit 0 after cancelled work, "user" wording, uncounted Bash tasks, results held back until exit, and the stale replay on `--resume`, with the repro, workarounds and suggested fixes. It is cross-linked on [#85066](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/85066#issuecomment-5892348970), next to the earlier follow-ups ([1](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/85066#issuecomment-5842704259), [2](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/85066#issuecomment-5885429221)).

## Incident 4: link-foundation/meta-language#196 ([review](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2302#issuecomment-5895702312))

The solve log and the bot log are private, so only sanitized excerpts are in the case study. Every symptom was traced to its cause:

| Symptom | Root cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No log on the failure; `RPC failed; HTTP 408` for a 165 MB log, and nothing on the PR | gh-upload-log 0.9.2 pushes once, without a retry; a failed attach was not reported | Retry with backoff, then upload complete line-aligned parts. If that also fails, a `Log Upload Failed` comment gives the reason and the log's location, never a partial log (#1678). Reported upstream as [gh-upload-log#45](https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-upload-log/issues/45) |
| Stop comment: "Review the attached working session log" when nothing was attached | Wording didn't depend on the upload | `logAttached` is passed through; the watch loop attaches before stopping |
| `Skipping: End comment (logs already attached…)` | An earlier iteration's attached log counted | Only the latest attempt counts |
| `solve` exited 0, so Telegram said "finished successfully" | A loop's failed AI session only posted a stop comment | The failure is recorded (`automation-failure.lib.mjs`), and the run exits 1 |
| "✅ finished successfully … recovered from out of memory" | Exit 0 above, plus a child OOM event read as "survived" | With exit 1 the run is resumed. The reply stays **🔄 Work session still in progress** until the recovery session ends |
| `out of memory — 9.8 GB of 11.7 GB RAM available` | Container `OOMKilled` read as exhaustion | Reads "container OOM event — a process in the task cgroup was killed earlier" |
| `Killed-session notice not posted: no-pull-request` | Only issue-started sessions looked a PR up | Falls back to the PR the session was started on |
| A recovery session would replace `📊 Session: 8ed87a4c-…` | The recovery session is tracked under its own id | The reply keeps the root session id and total duration and adds `🔁 Recovery session`. An in-place resume keeps the execution UUID and its single log |
| 1474 × `⚠️ Formatting error detected` | `message is not modified` and other non-formatting 400s were retried as plain text; `/queue` URLs with `_` opened an italic entity | Those are rethrown unchanged, and links render as `[owner/repo#N](url)`. The safety net stays for genuine formatting errors |

Tests (each fails on `main`): `tests/issue-2301-log-upload-resilience.test.mjs`, `tests/issue-2301-stop-comment-log-truth.test.mjs`, `tests/issue-2301-loop-failure-exit.test.mjs`, `tests/issue-2301-oom-resume-in-progress.test.mjs` (monitor replay of the PR-started OOM session: PR notice, 🔄 headline, root id, final ✅ edit), `tests/issue-2301-telegram-formatting-fallbacks.test.mjs`.

## Reproduction and verification

- `experiments/issue-2301-print-bg-ceiling/repro-ceiling.sh` runs live in about two minutes with Claude Code 2.1.284. Its captures are committed. It shows:
  - an 8 s ceiling killing a background agent (`success`, exit 0);
  - the Bash-only exit;
  - a raised ceiling that lets the same agent finish;
  - a same-session `--resume` with the prompt `solve` builds, whose turn reads the partial output, redoes the work in the foreground, and ends with `DONE`.
- `node experiments/issue-2301-print-bg-ceiling/replay-before-after.mjs`: the parser on `main` fails all three real fixtures with `Final tool result failed: The user doesn't want to proceed…`, while this branch schedules a continuation (10, 11 and 4 cancelled tasks).
- `tests/issue-2301-print-bg-ceiling.test.mjs` replays the three real sweeps and the three live captures. It covers:
  - the prompt content and the cap on the task list;
  - the attempt cap (the 5th resume still runs, then it stops);
  - the environment (background work on, ceiling 2400000 ms);
  - the Bash-only exit, `TaskStop`, a later main-thread turn and the stderr pattern.
- `tests/issue-2301-claude-execution.test.mjs` checks the same-session `--resume` through the real command wrapper. `tests/issue-2301-incomplete-claude-turn.test.mjs` checks the attempt cap, OOM classification and relaunch, the truthful notices and the memory limit.
- Local checks:
  - `npm test`: all 520 selected test files pass.
  - `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:duplication`, `npm run check:secrets`, `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`, `bash scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh`, `GITHUB_BASE_REF=main node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`.

No UI changes or screenshots are involved.

## CI follow-up

The first run on the implementation head failed the [dependency freshness gate](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/36216047631) with seven stale declarations. This PR now pins secretlint 13.0.6, use-m 8.16.4, command-stream 1.1.0, and links-notation 0.21.3, with matching lockfile and test expectations. The freshness check reports 148/148 current declarations. A live shell quoting regression and CLI smoke checks pass with the refreshed runtime packages.

A later run ([36534908254](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/36534908254)) failed the same gate after nine upstream releases. The pins are refreshed to:

- `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.6
- `start-command` 0.34.1
- `@sentry/node` and `@sentry/profiling-node` 11.1.0; `@sentry/bundler-plugins` 11.1.0 drops its `@babel/core` tree, which removes 31 lockfile entries
- `jscpd` 5.3.3
- `command-stream` 1.2.0
- `links-notation` 0.22.0

The freshness check now reports 151/151. The dependency, use-m and quoting tests, the duplication gate, and the `solve`/`hive --help` smoke runs pass with the new versions.

The latest run failed the gate once more after `command-stream` 1.3.0 was released. It is now pinned as a use-m version, the freshness check reports 151/151, and `experiments/command-stream-1.3.0-smoke.mjs` confirms it loads and quotes arguments correctly.

Run [36623926964](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/36623926964) failed the gate after `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.8 (a dependency refresh) was released. Both Dockerfiles now pin 0.26.8, and the freshness check reports 151/151.

CodeQL flagged two lines. The `/queue` escape helper not escaping `\` is a false positive: legacy Markdown only treats `\` as an escape before `_`, `*`, `` ` `` and `[`, so escaping it would show backslashes doubled. `experiments/issue-2301-codeql/backslash-escaping.mjs` demonstrates this, and a test pins it. The PR-notice test now asserts the exact `gh` arguments.

The first local full-suite run exposed an unrelated race in the existing issue #1823 process-group signal test: under load, it could signal its child before the child installed a SIGINT handler. The test now waits for the child's ready message; the case passed five consecutive isolated runs and a loaded full-suite run.

## Summary

- accept exact model IDs discovered from the installed Codex CLI or the merged router/provider catalogue instead of limiting execution to release-time aliases
- default Codex to the newest numeric `gpt-*-sol` exposed by the installed CLI, with `gpt-6-sol` as the bundled offline default
- preserve Claude Code's rolling `opus` alias for direct execution and resolve it to the newest concrete Opus ID for routed execution
- apply the same runtime-aware behavior to solve, hive, task, organizer, connection checks, agent-commander, and Telegram solve/hive/fix/task paths
- add current GPT-6 Sol/Luna/Reserve and Claude Opus 5.5 catalogue metadata, a changeset, multilingual docs, and a full evidence-backed case study

## Root cause

PR #2203 made live model discovery available to `/models`, but command validation still used only the bundled model map. Hive Mind could therefore display a newly released model and reject that same exact ID before the provider was invoked. Claude's rolling `opus` alias was also eagerly converted to a concrete release, defeating the vendor-managed default.

The fix keeps bundled aliases and typo suggestions as the first layer, then accepts only exact IDs reported by an authoritative runtime catalogue. Codex deliberately does not use a broad `gpt-*` regex, so `gpt-6-slo` still fails closed with a `gpt-6-sol` suggestion.

## Reproduction

Before this change, the following Telegram command was rejected locally even though `codex debug models` advertised `gpt-6-sol`:

```text
/codex <issue> --model gpt-6-sol --think xhigh --auto-merge
```

![Telegram rejecting GPT-6 Sol before the fix](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2290-9da101d37b7c/docs/case-studies/issue-2290/evidence/issue-screenshot.png?raw=true)

The regression test now proves current Sol/Opus behavior, direct and routed resolution, a hypothetical future `gpt-6.1-sol`, exact live-only IDs, and typo rejection.

## Verification

- `npm test` — all 502 selected test files passed
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run check:duplication`
- `npm run check:secrets`
- `bash scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh`
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`
- `node tests/docs-validation.mjs`
- `node tests/test-docs-language-sync.mjs`
- `node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs` with the PR base/head SHAs
- `node scripts/check-version.mjs`

## Investigation record

The [issue #2290 case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2290-9da101d37b7c/docs/case-studies/issue-2290/README.md) contains the evidence hashes, runtime catalogue, timeline, requirements, causal trace, alternatives, dependency analysis, security constraints, and verification matrix. No upstream issue was opened because the router and vendor CLIs already expose the required catalogue/alias behavior; the broken boundary was local to Hive Mind.

Fixes #2290

## Problem and resulting behavior

`solve --tool codex --model gpt-6.1-sol --think off` previously sent `model_reasoning_effort=none`, which the API rejected with HTTP 400. Effort selection now uses the selected model's exact capabilities: unsupported disabled thinking falls back to supported `auto` or the nearest tier (`low` for GPT-6.1 Sol), supported settings are preserved, and unknown capability sets use the configured model default.

## Changes

- Preserve effort arrays/defaults in live catalogues; reuse the shared one-hour cache and retain explicit CLI/router capabilities for future models. Runtime selection does not start a router or probe inference endpoints.
- Bundle verified current Codex capabilities and GPT-6.1 Sol's model ID, while preserving documented `none` support omitted from some CLI picker lists.
- Apply the shared resolver to native execution/resume, connection checks, agent-commander and organization planning. Filter planning capabilities by its existing `xhigh` ceiling before nearest-tier selection. Reuse existing Claude configuration in commander/planning to handle adaptive-only budgets and supported `xhigh` settings.
- Keep rollout-token caps only when the final effort is `ultra`; add verbose-only fallback/source diagnostics and a patch changeset.
- Refresh existing stale `command-stream`/`start-command`/`@dotenvx/dotenvx` pins and their fixtures to satisfy the repository's mandatory dependency-freshness check.

## Reproduction and tests

The minimal regression failed before the fix with `none !== low`. Separate tests reproduced an invalid adaptive-only Claude token budget and ignored gateway capabilities. New default-suite tests cover every nonempty effort subset, explicit/default/budget settings, future/unknown models, malformed/stale/offline metadata, gateway/direct isolation, custom CLI binaries and native new/resumed command construction. Final review added failing/passing planning-ceiling and connection rollout-cap regressions; the latter captures actual fake-CLI subprocess arguments. The reproducer and native tests do not run inference.

```sh
node tests/issue-2526-reasoning-effort.test.mjs
node tests/issue-2526-model-capabilities.test.mjs
node tests/issue-2526-native-codex.test.mjs
node experiments/issue-2526/reproduce.mjs
```

All 547 default-suite test files pass locally and in CI against final source commit `dec195ea`. CI also passes the GitHub integration test, Docker image/tool/nested-container verification, CodeQL, npm audit, lint, formatting, syntax, duplication, secrets, memory, documentation and release/dependency checks. All three implementation workflows are green: [Checks](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37381079901), [Security](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37381079552) and [link checking](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37381079578). [Latest PR checks](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2527/checks) cover the final evidence update.

## Investigation

[Case study, evidence and timeline](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2526-977f266926a4/docs/case-studies/issue-2526/README.md) · [Validation record](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2526-977f266926a4/docs/case-studies/issue-2526/validation.md) · [Upstream metadata report with reproducer, workaround and code suggestions](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44219#issuecomment-6000649081).

CI exposed five pre-existing stale dependency pins, which were refreshed. A subsequent command-stream release during final CI required one additional pin/fixture update. The complete local and CI suites pass with that update, and all 168 dependency declarations are current. The case study preserves failed reproductions, unavailable prior-solver evidence, runner-acquisition cancellations during GitHub's Actions outage, and the successful verification after service recovery. No test timeout or check was relaxed.

Fixes #2526.

## What

Turns off every AI tool's own cross-task memory, and Claude Code's auto-mode classifier, by default.

A hive-mind task is a disposable container that opens one pull request and is destroyed. The repository — commits, issues, pull requests, case studies — is meant to be the only memory it keeps, because it is the only memory a reviewer can see, correct, or revert. Every agentic CLI has since grown a private cross-session store that works against that, and the largest of them is not a file read but a whole second agent.

Closes #2178.

## What each tool actually ships

Read out of the installed binaries and bundles, not the documentation:

| Tool | Cross-session memory today |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code 2.1.246 | Per-project memory directory, team stores via `CLAUDE_MEMORY_STORES`, separately-gated org memory sync |
| Codex CLI 0.148.0 | `~/.codex/memories` + `memories_1.sqlite` behind the `memories` flag (stage: **stable**), plus `external_agent_memory_import` |
| Gemini CLI 0.51.0 | `experimental.autoMemory` starts a background `SkillExtractionAgent` that runs a Flash model over past sessions for up to 30 turns and writes a skills dir and a project `MEMORY.md`. `save_memory` was **removed** in this version |
| Qwen Code 0.7.1 | Still ships the `save_memory` tool it inherited from an earlier Gemini CLI |
| OpenCode 1.18.5 | None found |
| `agent` | None found |

The two "none found" rows are recorded in `TOOLS_WITHOUT_MEMORY_FEATURE` rather than omitted, and asserted by a test. "We looked and there was nothing" and "nobody looked" are different states, and only the first one stays true without someone re-checking.

## How

New `src/agent-memory-policy.lib.mjs` owns every knob, so `solve` and the Docker image baseline cannot disagree about what "off" means:

| Tool | Applied as | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| claude | `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ORG_MEMORY=1`, `autoMemoryEnabled: false`, `permissions.disableAutoMode: "disable"` | `claude-quiet-config.lib.mjs` (so `configure-claude` seeds the image) + the `ENV` block of all three Dockerfiles |
| codex | `-c features.memories=false -c features.external_agent_memory_import=false` | `codex.lib.mjs` and `agent-commander.lib.mjs` |
| gemini, qwen | `tools.exclude: ["save_memory"]`, `experimental.autoMemory: false` | merged into `~/.gemini/settings.json` / `~/.qwen/settings.json` before launch |
| opencode, agent | nothing to do | recorded, not silently skipped |

**On the classifier.** Claude Code decides auto-mode availability in a fixed order, and `permissions.disableAutoMode === "disable"` is checked *first* — before the plan circuit breaker, before the `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE` provider opt-in, before per-model availability. So it holds on every provider and model, which the env route does not. `defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` was already there and stays: it is what makes the classifier unnecessary, `disableAutoMode` is what makes it unreachable.

**Why settings files, not flags, for gemini/qwen.** Gemini 0.51 has no `--exclude-tools` (replaced by the policy engine); Qwen still accepts it. Passing a flag one of them does not know would fail at argument parsing. Both merge settings files and neither rejects unknown keys, and the merge unions arrays so an operator's own exclusions survive.

## The flag

`--agent-memory-disabled` defaults to `true`. `--no-agent-memory-disabled` opts out for codex/gemini/qwen — and when it does, the policy adds *no* arguments rather than arguments set to `true`.

It deliberately does **not** reach claude. Those switches are `ENV` lines in the image and settings written by `configure-claude`, and neither sees a `solve` argv. Rather than implying a control that is not there, the flag description, the options table (4 languages) and the case study all say the claude switches stay off regardless.

## What this does not do

- **Deletes nothing.** A `~/.codex/memories` directory that predates this is left on disk; the policy stops it being read and written, not existing.
- **Not verified end-to-end against a running CLI.** Knob names come from the shipped binaries and `codex features list`; the tests assert the wiring, not the effect. Confirming a routed `gemini` run really starts no extraction agent needs a live run with `--debug` and a look at the `[MemoryService]` log lines.
- **Leaves Codex's `guardian_approval` alone.** It looks classifier-shaped, but `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` already governs the approval path, and turning off a safety feature that costs us nothing was out of scope.

## Verification

- `tests/test-issue-2178-agent-memory-policy.mjs` — 22 new assertions: policy coverage for every `--tool` choice, both Claude gates, the codex overrides on both paths, settings-merge behaviour (operator keys survive, arrays union, compliant files are left byte-identical), and the failure paths (unwritable file → warning not throw; malformed JSON → replaced not crash).
- `tests/test-agent-commander-option.mjs` updated for the new codex args.
- `tests/test-claude-quiet-config.mjs` passes with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ORG_MEMORY` added to all three Dockerfiles.
- Full default suite: same 4 pre-existing failures as the untouched tree (`test-hive`, `test-sentry`, `test-solve`, `test-usage-limit`) — verified by stashing and re-running. No new failures.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run format`, file-line-limits, duplication check: clean.

Fixes #2189.

Follow-through PR for #2189. The first half shipped in [#2191](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2191) / `2.16.0` with **one requirement still open**: R2 asked for a killed session to be continued *in the same `$` session / container*, and `$` could not do that yet. This repository filed three upstream issues from that case study — [`link-foundation/start#162`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/162) (`--resume`), [`#164`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/164) (argv flattened with `join(' ')`), [`#165`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/165) (a V8 self-abort reported as `oomKilled=false`) — and **all three are delivered in `start-command@0.33.0`**.

The scope comment asked for the rest too:

> We need to finish this issue by actually updating https://github.com/link-foundation/start (as we reported issues there and they are now delivered) and all other dependencies we have in the repository. We also should see what changed, and use all relevant best practices from all our dependencies in all our supported languages.

So this PR closes R2, consumes what 0.33.0 delivers, and moves every other dependency forward — with the three that were *behaviour* changes handled rather than only bumped.

## 1. Same-container resume — requirement R2 (`78a6a679`)

`src/isolation-runner.resume.lib.mjs` wraps `$ --resume <id> [-- <command>]`, and `src/session-kill-resume.in-place.lib.mjs` makes it the **preferred** recovery path: the clone, the caches and the half-finished branch survive the kill instead of being rebuilt from scratch. When in-place resume is unavailable or refused, the previous behaviour — a fresh isolated run — still happens, and *why* is recorded on the session record (`killRecoveryInPlace`, `killRecoveryResumeMode`) and in the operator's report, so "resumed" and "restarted" are never conflated.

## 2. No more limbo executions (`df9dc818`)

The bot reconciles at startup with `$ --resume-all`: a container still running is re-attached to, and one that ended while unsupervised is finalized **with the exit code it actually had** — the state the incident report described as a session nobody could account for.

## 3. `$` refusals are read as refusals (`1211d554`)

`command-stream`'s `` $ `` **resolves** on a non-zero exit instead of throwing. Every `$` invocation therefore looked successful, including `$ --stop <unknown>`:

```
$ --stop u-9
Error: No execution found with UUID or session name: u-9     (stderr, exit 1)
→ reported to the operator as: stopped
```

Every call site now inspects the exit code. The resume wrappers additionally separate **an older `$` that does not know the verb** (`unsupported: true`, so callers keep their previous path) from **a genuine refusal** (`"Session … is still running"`), which are the same exit code and must not be treated the same way.

## 4. 0.33.0's kill hints are consumed (`60750f4a`)

`exitReason` and `memoryExhausted` from `$ --status` feed `describeKillCause` directly, so a runtime self-abort is named as out of memory from the supervisor's own answer — not only from log forensics as in #2191.

## 5. Every dependency updated, and what changed in them used

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `start-command` (both images) | 0.32.1 | **0.33.0** |
| `@changesets/cli` | 2.31.0 | **3.0.1** |
| `jscpd` | 4.0.5 | **5.1.2** |
| `@sentry/node`, `@sentry/profiling-node` | 10.62.0 | **10.73.0** |
| `prettier` | 3.8.5 | **3.9.6** |
| `agent-commander` | 0.8.0 | **0.10.1** |
| `dayjs` | 1.11.21 | **1.11.23** |
| `eslint` | 10.5.0 | **10.9.1** |
| `lint-staged` | 17.0.8 | **17.4.1** |
| `secretlint` (3 packages) | 13.0.2 | **13.0.5** |
| `lino-objects-codec` | 0.4.0 | **0.8.0** |
| `lino-i18n` | 0.1.1 | **0.2.0** |

Three of those were not just version numbers.

### `@changesets/cli` 2 → 3 breaks the release job

`changeset version` now **exits 1** when there are no unreleased changesets; 2.x warned and exited 0. From the installed 3.0.1 dist:

```js
if (changesets.length === 0) {
  logger.warn('No unreleased changesets found, exiting.');
  throw new ExitError(1);
}
```

The release workflow reads the changeset count *before* rebasing onto the remote, and the rebase can consume the very changesets the release decision was made on (a concurrent run versioned them first). Under 2.x that was a no-op; under 3.x it is a red release job for a repository in a perfectly fine state. `versionAndCommit` re-reads the count after the rebase and reports the already-published version through the existing `already_released` contract. Reproduced first, then fixed: `tests/test-issue-2189-changesets-3-version-guard.mjs`.

### `jscpd` 4 → 5 silently loosened the duplication gate

jscpd 5 is a Rust rewrite, and `skipComments` is an **unknown field** in it — it warns and falls back to `mode: mild`. `--debug` prints the merged config (`experiments/issue-2189/jscpd5-config-keys.sh`):

```
with "skipComments": true   →  Warning: unknown field `skipComments` …   "mode": "mild"
with "mode": "weak"         →  "mode": "weak"
```

`.jscpd.json` now says `"mode": "weak"`, which is what the old option means in 5.

### `@sentry/node` 10.71+ turns structured logs on by default — and they bypass `beforeSend`

`enableLogs` now defaults to `true`, and structured logs go through `beforeSendLog`; `beforeSend` never sees them. The redaction this repository relies on was therefore no longer covering everything that left the process. `src/instrument.sanitize.lib.mjs` is now shared between `beforeSend` and a new `beforeSendLog` hook, so both surfaces are scrubbed by the same code (`tests/test-issue-2189-sentry-log-sanitization.mjs`).

`node-pty` (new, via `agent-commander` 0.10's real-TUI capture) is denied a native build in `allowScripts`: it runs in a **separate spawned pty host** that this repository never launches headlessly, and the import path used here works without it.

Two more were checked and deliberately recorded as **not** affecting this repository, rather than claimed: dayjs 1.11.22's DST-offset fix is not reproducible with any call shape in this codebase (`experiments/issue-2189/dayjs-tz-dst.mjs` — identical offsets on both versions), while 1.11.23's `RangeError: Invalid time value` fix **is** (`experiments/issue-2189/dayjs-tz-invalid.mjs`).

## Case study

Everything above is written up with its evidence in **[`docs/case-studies/issue-2189/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2189-b28225043d62/docs/case-studies/issue-2189/README.md)** under **Dependency Follow-Through**, including the version table, the quoted upstream sources for each claim, and the one improvement deliberately deferred (jscpd 5's `--baseline-from-ref` / `--fail-on-new-clones`, which needs a baseline commit this PR should not pick).

## Tests

New:

- `tests/test-issue-2189-start-command-0.33.mjs` — the 0.33.0 status hints
- `tests/test-issue-2189-isolation-resume.mjs` — both resume wrappers end to end against a stub `$`, including the non-zero-exit and unsupported-verb paths
- `tests/test-issue-2189-same-container-resume.mjs` — R2, including every case in-place resume must refuse
- `tests/test-issue-2189-startup-resume-all.mjs` — startup reconciliation
- `tests/test-issue-2189-changesets-3-version-guard.mjs` — the changesets 3.0 release race
- `tests/test-issue-2189-sentry-log-sanitization.mjs` — `beforeSendLog` redaction

Two existing tests needed attention, for different reasons:

- `tests/test-issue-1980-docker-cleanup.mjs` asserts on the *source text* of the module holding `findStartCommandBinary`. That function moved to `src/start-command-cli.lib.mjs` — the resume wrappers need the `$` loader without importing the runner and creating a cycle — so the assertion was retargeted at the module that now holds the guarantee; the guarantee itself is unchanged.
- `tests/test-issue-2135-log-explosion.mjs` caught this PR's *own* new code. Its "every spawner reports the signal rather than interpolating a null code" guard forbids `exited with code ${code}` in spawner sources, and the first draft of the `$` wrappers wrote exactly that in `src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs` and `src/isolation-runner.resume.lib.mjs`. Both now report through `describeChildExit`, and `src/isolation-runner.resume.lib.mjs` was added to the guard's file list so the module this PR introduced is held to the same rule.

## Summary

The three post-#2154 Formal AI Hello World runs reached Formal AI 0.339.1 but produced no requested repository work: Agent recorded plans, Claude first ran `pwd`, Codex repeatedly ran bare `sudo`, all three PRs stayed empty, and each run spent its five-restart budget.

This PR fixes the Hive Mind side of that boundary without claiming the missing upstream executor:

- all six native-client adapters and Agent Commander now send Formal AI one shared, bounded repository objective without caller workflow commands, workspace paths, or copied feedback;
- explicit `planned_not_executed` terminal output becomes a failed tool result before mergeability retries;
- continue mode builds the canonical discovered pull request URL instead of labelling an issue URL as the PR;
- a patch changeset and regression coverage preserve the behavior for every client while native-model prompts remain unchanged.

Fixes #2158

## Root causes

| Root cause                                                   | Owner                          | Resolution                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Caller workflow text could win Formal AI intent routing      | Hive Mind boundary + Formal AI | Bounded provider-specific request locally; upstream follow-up on formal-ai#907 |
| Repository work intentionally ends as `planned_not_executed` | Formal AI                      | Surface as terminal failure locally; upstream follow-up on formal-ai#904       |
| Native CLI exit 0 was treated as task success                | Hive Mind                      | Shared result classifier at initial and restart chokepoints                    |
| Deterministic non-execution consumed five restarts           | Hive Mind                      | Failure classification occurs before mergeability handling                     |
| Continue mode reused the issue URL as the PR URL             | Hive Mind                      | Canonical `/pull/{number}` builder                                             |

## Reproduction

`experiments/issue-2158-formal-ai-prompt-boundary.mjs` runs real Codex against isolated Formal AI servers with the former flattened request and the new bounded request. Both production 0.339.1 and a release build of current Formal AI main 0.345.0 at `98cb3c8` produced the same comparison:

| Request                                        | Result                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Former 570-character workflow-prefixed request | Codex executes `/bin/bash -lc pwd`, exits 0, and reports the workspace                        |
| Bounded 281-character repository request       | No requested artifact changes; Formal AI exits 0 with `terminal_state "planned_not_executed"` |

The checked-in sanitized results are:

- `experiments/issue-2158-formal-ai-prompt-boundary-results.json` (0.339.1)

body:
Fixes #2146.

Formal AI is now the only model a Formal AI task can reach, it runs only while such a task exists, it is reachable only over a private internal Docker network, its memory survives every stop, and both the sidecar image and the bundled agentic CLIs refresh only while the host is idle. Every upstream prerequisite this needed has been filed, fixed, released, and is consumed here at its newest published version.

## What was wrong

The Aug 8 reproductions exposed three separate failures:

| Path           | Observed behavior                                                             | Root cause                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Agent          | A run requested Formal AI but contacted `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/messages` | Hive Mind interpolated `--model formalai/formal-ai --verbose` as one command-stream argv atom. Agent could not parse it, announced that it would use its default, and then failed open to `opencode/minimax-m2.5-free`. |
| Claude/Codex   | Five restarts per tool returned the same plan without implementing the issue  | The logs match Formal AI #904's pre-v0.326.1 plan-only signature. `--no-tool-check` suppressed the only version probe, so the exact runtime version was not recorded and a stale/unversioned binary was allowed to run. |
| GitHub summary | Formal AI's structured Lino plan collapsed into ordinary prose                | The working-session summary posted indented structured text without a code fence.                                                                                                                                       |

The restart controller itself behaved correctly: every Claude/Codex iteration still had an empty or placeholder-only diff, so Hive Mind retried five times and then failed.

## Formal AI is the only reachable model

Three independent layers, because any single one of them can be defeated by a future upstream change:

1. **Distinct argv atoms.** Every Agent flag is a separate argv element, including resume identifiers and stream-json flags, so `--model` can never arrive glued to another flag.
2. **An Agent CLI floor.** Agent only fails closed on a `--model` it cannot parse from **js-0.25.8** onwards ([agent#293](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/293) → [PR #294](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/pull/294)); earlier releases logged a CRITICAL record and then answered with their default model. A guard that reads that record can only stop the run after Agent has already decided, so `MIN_AGENT_FORMAL_AI_VERSION = '0.25.8'` makes a Formal AI task refuse to start below it.
3. **A streamed provider guard.** `AgentModelRoutingMismatch` terminates the process before further work if a Formal AI session announces an unparsable model flag or resolves any provider/model other than `formalai/formal-ai`.

Plus: `session.idle` is live-input state only — a prior streamed error is cleared only by `step_finish(reason=stop)` or an explicit successful result; the Formal AI runtime version is probed and logged unconditionally, even with `--no-tool-check`; and structured, indented result paragraphs are fenced at the GitHub-comment boundary while ordinary Markdown and existing fences are preserved.

## On-demand sidecar lifecycle

Formal AI used to exist only as an always-on Compose sibling — it ran when no Formal AI task did, it was never replaced, and Docker-isolated work sessions (created inside the Hive Mind container's own daemon) could not join its network at all, so they were handed a resolved IP address instead. The bot deployment now uses a lease-counted, on-demand sidecar ([`src/formal-ai-sidecar.lib.mjs`](src/formal-ai-sidecar.lib.mjs)):

- A Formal AI task is identified from the task's parsed `--model`, not from the selected CLI tool.
- The first such task creates the `--internal` network, the memory volume and the container **inside the closed per-session start gate**, before any agent process exists. Concurrent tasks share one container under explicit leases keyed on the session UUID; the last release stops it.
- Nothing is published to the host — `buildFormalAiSidecarRunArgs` emits no `-p`/`--publish`, and only Formal AI task containers are attached, with `docker network connect` in that same gate ([`src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs`](src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs)).
- Reconciliation re-derives truth from Docker rather than trusting the durable store: an unseen container gets a bounded one-hour launch grace, a container once seen and now gone is stale immediately, so a crashed task cannot pin the sidecar forever.
- `hive-mind-formal-ai-memory` is mounted at `/home/box/.formal-ai` and no code path issues `docker volume rm` — memory survives every stop, failure and rollback.

`docker-compose.yml` keeps the always-on shape as the documented exception — Compose has no bot process and no Docker socket to manage a lifecycle with — and sets `HIVE_MIND_FORMAL_AI_SIDECAR=0` so no second sidecar is started next to it. Both shapes share the `hive-mind-formal-ai-memory` volume name and the `link-assistant-formal-ai` alias, so memory survives a move between them.

`start-command` can name a network at launch since 0.31.0 ([start#154](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/154) → [PR #155](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/pull/155)) and, since 0.32.0 ([start#156](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/156) → [PR #157](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/pull/157)), can repeat `--network` so a task could join the default bridge _and_ the internal sidecar network at launch. The images pin `start-command@0.32.1`. Hive Mind still attaches tasks itself with `docker network connect` inside the closed start gate, deliberately: the released upstream implementation of repeatable `--network` is the identical `docker create` → `docker network connect` → `docker start` sequence, the gate is already held for the writable-layer baseline, and the in-repo attach stays fail-closed on every installed start-command version instead of silently collapsing to one network on a pre-0.32.0 parser.

## Idle-only updates

Images now pin only the **bootstrap** Formal AI version (0.339.1, the newest release). [`src/formal-ai-updater.lib.mjs`](src/formal-ai-updater.lib.mjs) adopts newer digests while idle, using the persisted-memory upgrade contract delivered by [formal-ai#982](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/982) → [PR #985](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/985) → [v0.336.0](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/releases/tag/v0.336.0): pull → side-effect-free `memory upgrade-status` → locked/backed-up/atomic `memory migrate` with a JSON receipt → boot the candidate → check `/health`'s `memory.compatible` → stop it again. Any failure restores `backup_path` and verifies its SHA-256 from the receipt. Two extra properties the contract does not itself promise are checked: the preflight's `source_sha256` is compared against the receipt's `original_sha256` (a preflight that mutated the file is its own rollback-worthy stage), and the candidate is stopped after verification so a successful idle update leaves the host idle.

Both `memory` subcommands print JSON on **stdout** and _then_ exit nonzero when they refuse (`src/cli_memory.rs`), so the parser is applied to failed commands too and `refusal_code`/`refusal_reason` is surfaced instead of "exit status 1".

[`src/agentic-cli-updater.lib.mjs`](src/agentic-cli-updater.lib.mjs) does the same for the bundled CLIs: it acts only when the live task list is empty, probes each target with `--version`, skips CLIs absent from the image, resolves published versions with a throttled `npm view`, refreshes Claude with its own `claude update` and the Bun-installed CLIs with `bun install -g <package>@latest`. `@link-assistant/hive-mind` (it owns the running process) and `start-command` (pinned by the Dockerfile) are asserted exclusions. All three duties run from one tick in [`src/formal-ai-maintenance.lib.mjs`](src/formal-ai-maintenance.lib.mjs) in the only safe order — reconcile-and-stop, image update, CLI refresh — each best-effort so maintenance never takes the bot down.

## Upstream reports filed from this incident

| Report                                                                                                    | Outcome                                                                                | Consumed here as                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [agent#293](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/293) — `--model` fail-open                     | [PR #294](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/pull/294) → js-0.25.8                | `MIN_AGENT_FORMAL_AI_VERSION`; a Formal AI task refuses to start below it      |
| [formal-ai#982](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/982) — no safe memory upgrade contract | [PR #985](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/985) → v0.336.0             | preflight/migrate/verify/rollback; `FORMAL_AI_MEMORY_CONTRACT_MINIMUM_VERSION` |
| [start#154](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/154) — no Docker network at launch            | [PR #155](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/pull/155) → js-0.31.0 / rust-0.18.0 | pinned in `Dockerfile`/`Dockerfile.dind`; used for the sidecar                 |

All three are closed as completed and consumed here. Re-reading the _delivered_ releases against what this PR actually depends on, and reading the first full CI run this branch ever got, surfaced four more follow-ups, now filed rather than kept as private knowledge:

- [agent#295](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/295) — the provider guard has to discriminate on `message === 'using explicit provider/model'` (`js/src/cli/model-config.js:118`). Rewording that string is non-breaking upstream and would silently disable a safety guard, so it asks for a typed `model_resolved` event with `source` and `matchesRequest`. Not a blocker: it is the third layer, and the two in front of it stop the incident on their own.
- [start#156](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/156) — PR #155 shipped a single-valued `--network`, and `docker run --network` replaces the default bridge, so no single-network invocation can express "reach GitHub _and_ the sidecar". **Closed as completed**: delivered on Aug 10 by [PR #157](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/pull/157) and fully released the same day as `js-v0.32.0`/`js-v0.32.1` once the next item was fixed. This PR pins `start-command@0.32.1`.
- [start#160](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/160) — the integration test that came with #157 probed internet egress with `https://api.github.com`, which rate limits unauthenticated callers per source IP; on a shared Actions runner it answered `403`, BusyBox `wget --spider` reported that as failure, and the JavaScript release job was skipped. Reproduced locally and filed with the one-line fix. **Closed as completed the same day**: the fix landed, [`js-v0.32.0`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/releases/tag/js-v0.32.0) published at 12:32 UTC, and [`js-v0.32.1`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/releases/tag/js-v0.32.1) / [`rust-v0.19.2`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/releases/tag/rust-v0.19.2) followed at 17:42.
- [formal-ai#988](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/988) — from 0.333.0 `cargo install formal-ai --locked` failed on a stock Rust image: the tree reached `native-tls` → `openssl-sys`, which needs `pkg-config` and the OpenSSL headers. Found by this PR's own `docker-pr-check`, reproduced locally, and traced to two one-line manifests: [web-capture#151](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/151) (`reqwest 0.12` with default features) and [browser-commander#77](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/77) (`fantoccini 0.21` with default features, `default = ["native-tls"]`). **Closed as completed**: [v0.339.0](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/releases/tag/v0.339.0) removed `openssl-sys` from formal-ai's `Cargo.lock`, so the locked install can no longer reach the failure. The two root-cause issues remain open, so the four builder stages keep `pkg-config`/`libssl-dev`/`OPENSSL_STATIC=1` as defense in depth — inert while `openssl-sys` is absent, and load-bearing again if a future release drags it back in.

Every field this PR reads was re-verified against the **released** Formal AI sources (`src/memory/upgrade.rs`, `src/cli_memory.rs`, `src/server.rs`, `src/shared_memory.rs`) rather than against the issue text, because consuming a contract from its proposal is how integrations drift — first against v0.337.0, and again against v0.339.1 before moving the bootstrap pin: three of the four files are byte-identical between the tags, and `upgrade.rs` only adds an explicit advisory-lock release, so every contract claim holds unmodified.

The mandatory pause rule from #2146 therefore no longer applies — the blockers it was waiting on are delivered, and this PR consumes the newest published release of each (formal-ai 0.339.1, agent js-0.25.8, start js-0.32.1 / rust-0.19.2).

## Regression coverage

- [`tests/test-issue-2146-formal-ai-support.mjs`](tests/test-issue-2146-formal-ai-support.mjs) — argv atoms, provider drift, strong completion, version floor, Markdown fencing, idempotence.
- [`tests/test-issue-2146-formal-ai-lifecycle.mjs`](tests/test-issue-2146-formal-ai-lifecycle.mjs) — lease counting, internal network, no published ports, reconciliation grace/staleness, volume survival.
- [`tests/test-issue-2146-idle-updates.mjs`](tests/test-issue-2146-idle-updates.mjs) — busy-host refusal, rollback at the `verify` and `preflight-side-effect` stages, refusal payload shapes, CLI-updater exclusions.
- [`tests/test-issue-2130-formal-ai-runtime.mjs`](tests/test-issue-2130-formal-ai-runtime.mjs) — a stale binary is rejected before a server starts.
- [`tests/test-codex-support.mjs`](tests/test-codex-support.mjs) — the Agent floor is proven with a `PATH` stub that records every non-`--version` invocation: on 0.25.7 `validateAgentConnection('formal-ai')` returns false **and the stub is never invoked**, so the outdated CLI never gets the chance to answer with another model; on 0.25.8 the probe is recorded. Asserting only the boolean would pass against an implementation that refuses _after_ sending the request.

The lifecycle and update suites run against [`tests/formal-ai-docker-simulator.mjs`](tests/formal-ai-docker-simulator.mjs), an in-memory Docker daemon modelling containers, `internal` networks, volumes, image digests, `/health` payloads and the two `formal-ai memory` subcommands including their stdout-then-nonzero refusals — deterministic, and needing no daemon, registry or Formal AI image in CI.

## Case study and preserved evidence

[`docs/case-studies/issue-2146/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2146/) contains the timeline, the requirement matrix across #2119/#2130/#2146 and both review comments, five root causes, the nine lifecycle invariants with the module and test that enforce each, the field-by-field verification against v0.337.0 (re-checked against v0.339.1), alternatives considered, an implementation map, the verification procedure, remaining limits, and a "What is left" section.

The data bundle includes 16 sanitized logs, authenticated Gist snapshots, issue/PR/comment/review API captures, and SHA-256 hashes. Every JSON file parses, every gzip archive passes its integrity check, and every tool-log hash matches [`MANIFEST.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-2146/MANIFEST.md). No screenshots: this is not a UI change and the linked discussions contained no images.

## What is left

Nothing in issue #2146 or in the review comments on this PR is outstanding here, and no requirement is waiting on an upstream fix. Every issue this work filed that could have blocked it is closed as completed and its release is consumed here: [start#156](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/156), [start#160](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/160), and [formal-ai#988](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/988). Three follow-up reports remain open upstream — none blocks this PR, each has a working downstream answer, and the case study records why:

- https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/295 — model routing should be a typed event, not an English log string; the guard here works against every released 0.25.8+ build and is the third defensive layer.
- https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/151 — `reqwest` default features pull `native-tls`/`openssl-sys` into consumers; the symptom is already fixed downstream in formal-ai 0.339.0, and the builder stages keep the OpenSSL packages as inert defense in depth.
- https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/77 — the same root-cause class via `fantoccini` default features; covered by the same defense in depth.

Known, deliberate limits:

- Already-built Docker isolation images keep the CLI versions baked in at build time until rebuilt. The review explicitly allowed either approach; the in-container path was chosen because it cannot spend task time or drift between concurrent tasks.
- The memory migration path is exercised against a simulated v1→v2 migration, because 0.339.1 (like 0.336.0–0.338.x before it) reads schema 1 and 2 and targets 2, so no real migration is pending yet.
- One shared sidecar per host is what makes memory shared and persistent, so Formal AI tasks are not isolated from each other's memory.
- The one item that cannot be closed from this repository is the original behavioral complaint: Formal AI's agent mode produced a plan and no code in every reproduction. That is tracked upstream on its own coding-capability track ([#848](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/848), [#904](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/904)). What Hive Mind can do — refuse to call it a success, refuse to retry it forever, and refuse to quietly finish the work on another model — it now does.

## Checks

- `npm test` (default suite), `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:duplication`, `git diff --check`
- issue-2146 lifecycle, idle-update, support and runtime suites, plus `tests/test-codex-support.mjs`
- case-study JSON, gzip, checksum, and credential-signature validation
- one release changeset (`.changeset/formal-ai-2146.md`, `minor` — the sidecar lifecycle and the idle updaters are new backwards-compatible features)

body: Fixes #2119. ## What was wrong Three `hive-mind solve --model formal-ai` runs on 2026-07-30, one per `--tool`, produced **zero lines of source code** between them — and Hive Mind reported all three as successes. The AI side of that is Formal AI's problem and is [reported upstream](#upstream). This pull request is about our side: **every signal Hive Mind published about those runs was wrong.** | Run | Tool | Language | What was published | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [`019fb330-00e1-…`](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-00e1-73b9-955e-f357a1600d5b/pull/2) | `agent` | Scala | `Provider: OpenCode Zen`, `Token usage: 0 input, 0 output`, 11 AI sessions under a limit of 5, exit **0** | | [`019fb330-fa49-…`](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-fa49-7c9d-a664-b7ea33bb698a/pull/2) | `claude` | Kotlin | `Calculated by Anthropic: $0.252315` for a free model, then `## ✅ Ready to merge` on an empty diff | | [`019fb331-c107-…`](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb331-c107-78c7-8ff6-9f127a3c593c/pull/2) | `codex` | Rust | A pull request containing only our own `.gitkeep`, described as `1 file(s) modified` | For contrast, the same generator in 2025 produced two-file, 45–81 line pull requests with a conventional model. The pipeline works when the model answers; what it cannot do is notice when the model does not. ## What this changes Thirteen defects, each with a regression test. Every fix is applied across **all six** tools (`claude`, `agent`, `opencode`, `codex`, `qwen`, `gemini`), not only where the symptom was observed. The Docker images also pin Formal AI 0.317.0, which contains the upstream generalized recovery fix. **Attribution and cost** — `src/formal-ai-pricing.lib.mjs` is now the single source of the provider name and the zero-cost override, consulted at the cost boundary of all six tools plus `agent-commander` and the cost renderer. - D1 `Provider: OpenCode Zen` / `Calculated by Anthropic` → **`Link.Assistant`**, because the tool that ran says nothing about who served the tokens - D2 `$0.252315` for a free model → **`$0.00`** - D3 `Public pricing estimate: unknown` → **`$0.00 (Free model)`** **Telemetry** — `src/json-stream.lib.mjs` frames records by balanced JSON values instead of by newlines, so pretty-printed, concatenated and chunk-split records all parse. - D4 `Token usage: 0 input, 0 output` for a session that used 44 511 tokens → real counts, for every tool - D12 the credential sanitizer redacting `"tokens": [REDACTED]` and JSON braces → counters and structure survive, secrets still do not **The restart loop** — `src/auto-restart-budget.lib.mjs` replaces two independent loops that shared one flag. - D5 `Auto-restart 1/5` … `5/5` **and then** `Auto-restart triggered (iteration 1)` … `(iteration 5)` — 11 AI sessions under `--auto-restart-max-iterations 5` → one budget, one `N/M` label - D6 exhausting the budget exited **0** with the work undone → fails visibly, with auto-commit on fail recovery, exit **1** - D11 `?? .formal-ai/` counted as user changes, re-created by every restart so the blocker never cleared → `src/ai-tool-scratch.lib.mjs` excludes AI scratch state via `.git/info/exclude` **Not calling nothing a success** - D8 `- 1 file(s) modified` for an empty net diff → measured from the diff, not from per-commit sums - D9 `## ✅ Ready to merge` on a pull request that changes nothing → an empty diff is a blocker, not a green light - D13 the solver's own `.gitkeep` / `CLAUDE.md` placeholder counted as the AI's work → matched by generated content (a repository's own `.gitkeep` still counts) and reported as `placeholderOnly` - D10 a working-session summary made of `pwd` output, leaking `/tmp/gh-issue-solver-…` → summaries carry facts or say they have none - D7 PR titles published as `'Implement Hello World in Scala'`, quotes included → command-stream escapes interpolations itself; the redundant quotes are gone everywhere they appeared ## Tests Nine new suites, all in the default suite (`npm test`, currently 368 files): `test-formal-ai-pricing-2119` · `test-agent-stream-json-2119` · `test-token-telemetry-sanitization-2119` · `test-auto-restart-budget-2119` · `test-empty-pull-request-2119` · `test-shell-quoting-2119` · `test-working-session-summary-2119` · `test-ai-tool-scratch-2119` · `test-formal-ai-uniform-tools-2119` The last one is the anti-regression net for the whole class: it asserts that all five stream parsers import the shared framer, all six tools reach the formal-ai pricing path, and all four Docker image definitions pin Formal AI 0.317.0, so a tool or image variant cannot silently retain a divergent implementation. Final verification after merging current `main`: all 368 default test files passed under Node 24, together with ESLint, Prettier, MJS syntax checks, file-line limits, duplication analysis, changeset validation, and `git diff --check`. ## Case study [`docs/case-studies/issue-2119/`](./docs/case-studies/issue-2119) holds the reconstruction the issue asked for: minute-by-minute timelines of the three runs, an inventory of all six `konard/test-hello-world-*` repositories (2025 baseline vs 2026), the requirement-by-requirement table, root cause and fix for each of the thirteen defects, the two deliberate non-changes, where the data was insufficient and what instrumentation was added, and the libraries considered for the JSON framing (jsonhilo, concatjson, clarinet, json-stream-es, stream-json) with the reason we did not use them. Raw evidence — logs, issue/PR JSON, diffs, gist URLs — is archived under `data/`. ## Upstream resolved and shipped - **[link-assistant/formal-ai#879](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/879)** was fixed by [Formal AI PR #881](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/881) and released in 0.316.1. It adds a seed-driven, bounded recovery ladder with cross-run learning, requires observable non-scratch workspace effects, fails closed on public endpoint diversion, and emits completion telemetry across all six clients. Hive Mind now pins the current 0.317.0 release in every Docker image. - **[link-assistant/agent#285](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/285)** was fixed by [Agent PR #286](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/pull/286) and published in npm package 0.25.4. Unknown models now get the full prompt with an explicit logged default, product identity is centralized, and session versions come from the package manifest. Hive Mind's image install resolves to the current 0.25.5 package.

## Summary

Fixes #2027.

Makes `gpt-5.6-sol` the default model for `--tool codex` and makes the thinking/effort levels predictable and consistent across both `codex` and `claude`. By default, both tools run the model as-is with **no thinking level enforced**.

## What changed (per requirement)

- **R1 — Default to GPT-5.6 Sol.** `defaultModels.codex` is now `gpt-5.6-sol`. `primaryModelNames.codex` leads with `gpt-5.6-sol`, and `gpt-5.5` is the first entry in `CODEX_DEFAULT_FALLBACK_CHAIN`, so environments whose local Codex catalog has not exposed Sol yet still resolve a working model.
- **R2 — All other models still supported.** The full Codex allowlist and fallback chain are preserved; no model IDs were removed. Regression tests assert the catalog still validates.
- **R3 — Predictable Codex levels.** `--think` maps 1:1 to Codex `model_reasoning_effort`: `off`→`none`, `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`ultra`/`max` identity. `xhigh` is natively supported (confirmed by `codex debug models`); `max` sits above `xhigh`; `ultra` is GPT-5.6 Sol's multi-agent mode. `--think ultra` is always paired with a `rollout_token_budget` cap (`500000` default, override via the new `--rollout-token-budget`). Budget-derived effort caps at `xhigh` so `max`/`ultra` require an explicit `--think`.
- **R4 — Align Claude.** Added the `ultra` level (ultracode-class): `thinkLevelToEffortLevel` clamps `ultra` to the highest supported effort (`max`, else `xhigh`, else `high`), `getThinkingLevelToTokens` maps `ultra` to the max token budget, and the thinking prompt emits `Ultrathink.`.
- **R5 — No thinking by default.** With no `--think`, `resolveCodexReasoningEffort` returns `reasoning_effort=none` (source `default`) and Claude adds no effort/budget overrides.
- **R6 — Case study.** Research data and analysis collected under [`docs/case-studies/issue-2027`](docs/case-studies/issue-2027/README.md), including the authoritative `codex debug models` output and GPT-5.6 Sol reasoning notes.

## Reproduction / verification

- `tests/test-codex-support.mjs` — default `gpt-5.6-sol`, primary/fallback ordering, runtime fallback to `gpt-5.5` when Sol is absent, and the identity reasoning mapping (`ultra` with `rolloutTokenBudget=500000`, overridable to `250000`; `max` with no budget; `xhigh` budget cap; `none` default/off).
- `tests/test-agent-commander-option.mjs` — Codex extra args for `xhigh`, `max`, and `ultra` (the latter appends `rollout_token_budget`), plus a custom `--rollout-token-budget` override.

- Docs sync/validation: `tests/test-docs-language-sync.mjs`, `tests/docs-validation.mjs`, `tests/test-docs-options-sync.mjs`.

All of the above pass locally (run with `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`/`CLAUDE_EFFORT` unset, since the CI/dev harness leaks those env vars into unrelated Claude-effort tests).

## Notes

- The local `codex debug models` (`codex-cli 0.142.5`) does not yet list the GPT-5.6 preview models; hive-mind's registry already accepts them (added in #1992), so this change is the default flip plus the thinking-level work.

## Summary

Fixes #1990. Two long-running `solve --tool codex` tasks running under **detached
Docker isolation** reported **SUCCESS (`Exit Code: 0`)** to `solve`, the Telegram
bot, and the `start-command` (`$`) tracker — while in reality both containers had

**Root cause:** `solve`'s per-tool success determination trusted the **process
exit code** alone. A machine-readable AI run (`codex exec --json`, and the
gemini/qwen stream-json equivalents) can exit `0` even when its session was
interrupted mid-run. A healthy run always closes with a **terminal completion
event**; an interrupted one does not — but we never checked for it.

Confirmed in both raw logs: `turn.started` = 1, **`turn.completed` = 0**,
`turn.failed` = 0 — the Codex turn never closed, yet the process exited `0`.

## What changed

A run is reported as success **only if** it exits `0` **and** emits its
tool-specific terminal completion event:

| Tool | Terminal signal | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| **codex** | paired `turn.started`/`turn.completed` (or `turn.failed`) | exit code only | `getCodexCompletionHealth()` (`src/codex-health.lib.mjs`) |
| **claude** | final `result` event | already gated | unchanged |
| **gemini** | terminal `result` event | exit code only | `getTerminalEventCompletionHealth()` (`src/tool-run-health.lib.mjs`) |
| **qwen** | terminal `result` event | exit code only | `getTerminalEventCompletionHealth()` |
| **opencode** | none verified | exit code only | intentionally **not** gated (documented rationale) |

- **Not registered as success** (R1): `!healthy` → `success:false`.
- **Context-preserving retry** (R2): each tool sets `argv.resume = sessionId` on
  failure, so the outer loop resumes the same AI session — like `--tool claude`.
- **Failure preserves the docker filesystem** (R3): `success:false` → inner
  `solve` exits non-zero → docker footer `Exit Code: 1` → isolation reports
  failure → container retained.
- **#1955 echo-trap safe**: disk-exhaustion strings are surfaced as *diagnostics
  only*, never an independent failure gate (Session B's only "No space left on
  device" string is an echoed file's contents, not a real error).

## Reproduce / tests

```bash
node tests/test-issue-1990-codex-incomplete-session-false-success.mjs   # codex gate
node tests/test-issue-1990-multitool-incomplete-session.mjs             # gemini + qwen + shared helper
node tests/test-issue-1955-codex-fixture-false-positive.mjs             # echo-trap guard intact
```

Each test drives the real tool function with a mocked `$` that yields an exit-0
stream **missing** its terminal event, and asserts `success:false` +
`incompleteSession:true` + `argv.resume` preserved; a stream that reaches its
terminal event still succeeds.

## Case study & upstream

- **Deep analysis + raw logs:** [`docs/case-studies/issue-1990/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-1990-205daff5585b/docs/case-studies/issue-1990) — reconstructed timeline, full requirement decomposition, per-problem root causes, prior-art reuse.
- **Upstream enhancement filed:** [link-foundation/start#144](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/144) — `start` correctly relayed the inner exit code (the primary fix is here), but it was asked to surface `State.OOMKilled` and preserve abnormally-terminated container filesystems as defense-in-depth. Our in-repo gate is the workaround referenced there.

Fixes #1990.
title: Fix: docker-isolated runs falsely reported as success when the AI session is cut off mid-run (#1990)

## Summary

Fixes #1230

When the solver encounters an empty repository (no commits) with direct write access, branch creation fails because \`origin/main\` has no commits to branch from. The existing empty repository handling only covered the **fork path** (HTTP 403 "Empty repositories cannot be forked").

This PR adds:
- **New \`--auto-init-repository\` CLI option** (default: \`false\`) that automatically creates a simple README.md in empty repositories
- **Empty repository detection** in the direct access path via \`detectEmptyRepository()\`
- **Auto-initialization** that reuses the existing \`tryInitializeEmptyRepository()\` function
- **Issue comment posting** when empty repo cannot be resolved (mirrors fork-path behavior)
- **Improved error messages** that suggest \`--auto-init-repository\` when empty repos are encountered
- **Case study documentation** in \`docs/case-studies/issue-1230/\`
- **Documentation updates** in \`README.md\` and \`docs/CONFIGURATION.md\`

### How it works

1. After cloning, \`verifyDefaultBranchAndStatus()\` detects the repository is empty (no HEAD, no remote branches)
2. If \`--auto-init-repository\` is enabled and user has write access:
   - Creates a README.md via GitHub API (reusing existing \`tryInitializeEmptyRepository()\`)
   - Waits for GitHub to process, then re-fetches
   - Checks out the new default branch and continues normally
   - **No comment is posted** on the issue (no user action needed)
3. If the flag is NOT enabled: shows clear error message suggesting the flag + **posts a comment on the issue** informing the user
4. If initialization fails: shows actionable guidance + **posts a comment on the issue** with fix suggestions

### Issue comment behavior

The comment-to-issue behavior follows the same pattern as the existing fork-path code in \`solve.repository.lib.mjs\`:
- Comment is posted via \`gh issue comment\` when empty repo is detected and cannot be resolved
- Comment suggests using \`--auto-init-repository\` flag or manually initializing the repository
- Comment is **NOT** posted when auto-init succeeds (no user action required)
- Comment errors are non-critical and silently ignored

### Example usage

\`\`\`bash
# Auto-initialize empty repository before solving
solve https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/1 --auto-init-repository
\`\`\`
